name: Isosurface extraction
text:
# Isosurface extraction

Also called: contouring, polygonization, marching cubes family

## Overview
Isosurface extraction converts a discretized scalar field into a polygonal mesh (typically triangles) representing the locus of points where the field equals a specific threshold (isovalue) [S1, S5, unofficial]. It solves the problem of visualizing implicit 3D structures by transforming volumetric data into explicit surface geometry suitable for rendering or simulation [S6, unofficial]. Unlike [Blocky meshing](31-blocky-meshing.md), which produces voxel-aligned "cuberille" meshes, isosurface methods generate smooth, curved approximations by interpolating within cells [S1, unofficial][S12].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md) (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers. The core mechanism involves traversing the grid cells and evaluating the data to determine which parts of the domain constitute the surface [G].

1.  **Domain Traversal**: The algorithm iterates over the volume data structure [G]. For regular grids, this often involves checking each cell or voxel [G].
2.  **Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations. In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md]. In [blocky meshing](#31-blocky-meshing.md), this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
3.  **Primitive Generation**: Geometric primitives (vertices, edges, faces) are generated based on the determined surface locations [G].
4.  **Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].

## Subtopics

### [Advancing Front Framework for Implicit Surfaces](819-advancing-front-framework-for-implicit-surfaces.md)
Constructs a triangulated mesh by growing a front across the implicit surface, starting from a seed point and extending it edge-by-edge. Unlike numerical simulation meshing which starts with well-defined domain representations and increases primitive dimension, this method operates without a pre-defined description of volume components, requiring the algorithm to dynamically chart the reconstructed surface.

### [Isosurface Extraction API](836-isosurface-extraction-api.md)
Provides a high-level interface for extracting a manifold triangular mesh from a continuous implicit scalar field defined by a user-supplied function, rather than a pre-computed discrete grid. It sets itself apart from standard grid-based methods like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by accepting a callable function `func(x,y,z)` directly, handling gradient estimation via finite differences if not provided, and supporting adaptive refinement through octree depth parameters.

### [Minimal Area Triangulation for Polygons](859-minimal-area-triangulation-for-polygons.md)
Decomposes non-convex or complex 3D polygons (isopolygons) resulting from isosurface extraction into a set of triangles, specifically minimizing the total area of the resulting triangles to reduce visual artifacts. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by operating on the final polygonal boundary rather than voxel cells, and from [Dual Contouring and Surface Nets](6319-dual-contouring-and-surface-nets.md) by optimizing for minimal surface area of the triangulation itself rather than vertex position optimization.

### [VESTA](900-vesta.md)
Constructs isosurfaces by generating N-cycles from 3-cell configurations, resolving ambiguities at voxel face junctures to prevent surface holes, unlike the original Marching Cubes Algorithm. [VESTA](#900-vesta.md) differs from template-based methods like Marching Cubes by using a single building block based on vector [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md), ensuring the surface is non-degenerate, volume-enclosing, and hole-free without requiring post-processing repair.

### [Isosurface extraction on arbitrary polyhedral grids](951-isosurface-extraction-on-arbitrary-polyhedral-grids.md)
Extracts isosurfaces from scalar fields defined on arbitrary polyhedral cells (convex, non-convex, planar, or non-planar) by approximating the surface locally at each cell as a polygonal surface (isopolygon). It solves the topological inconsistencies and holes inherent in standard Marching Cubes on ambiguous faces by treating face boundaries systematically using general polygon tracing rules, rather than relying on predefined [configuration tables](#1484-marching-cubes-face-generation.md). Unlike Marching Tetrahedra, it operates directly on arbitrary polyhedra without decomposing them into tetrahedra.

### [Extended CLCIR PLIC Reconstruction](954-extended-clcir-plic-reconstruction.md)
Reconstructs a Piecewise Linear Interface Concept (PLIC) plane for Volume of Fluid (VOF) simulations on arbitrary polyhedral grids by extracting an isosurface from an interpolated scalar field and computing a weighted normal vector. It is distinguished from standard VOF methods by its explicit geometric flux calculation via isosurface extraction and from pure isosurface methods by its integration into a VOF advection loop with volume conservation enforcement.

### [Multi-Isosurface Extraction](1162-multi-isosurface-extraction.md)
Extracts and renders multiple isosurfaces from the same scalar volume data simultaneously by running the Marching Cubes algorithm for each selected isovalue. Unlike single isosurface extraction, this method requires managing multiple triangle lists and potentially multiple rendering passes or state changes for different isovalue colors. It builds on [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md) by extending the extraction loop to iterate over a user-defined list of isovalues rather than a single scalar threshold.

### [Convex Contouring with Decision Trees](1201-convex-contouring-with-decision-trees.md)
A table-driven isosurface extraction technique that generates topologically consistent surfaces where the negative space inside each cell is locally convex. Unlike [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md), which may produce disconnected or non-convex negative space within cells, Convex Contouring ensures that the convex hull of the negative space is preserved, enabling fast collision detection on the triangulated isosurface. It distinguishes itself from other cell-based methods by using pre-computed decision trees to dynamically select the correct triangulation from a set of candidates based on edge intersection positions, rather than relying on static lookup tables that ignore magnitude information.

### [Octree-based Isosurfacing](1247-octree-based-isosurfacing.md)
Replaces the uniform Cartesian grid with an adaptive octree spatial discretization for [surface extraction](#29-surface-extraction.md) algorithms such as Marching Cubes and Dual Contouring. This approach enables variable resolution, refining only where the surface geometry demands it, but it sacrifices the topological guarantees of uniform grids, potentially introducing cracks in the resulting mesh if the octree is not sufficiently adapted to the surface.

### [High-Dimensional Triangulation Tables](1336-high-dimensional-triangulation-tables.md)
Generates [precomputed triangulation tables](#4800-marching-cubes-lookup-table.md) for isosurface extraction in $n$-dimensional hypercubes. It addresses the excessive simplex count produced by recursive contour-meshing, which requires subdividing 4-cells into 4-simplices before contouring, analogous to breaking a cube into five or six tetrahedra in 3D. Unlike recursive decomposition, this method constructs an $n$-polytope via convex hulls to determine the isosurface directly within the hypercube, ensuring consistent triangulation between adjacent faces.

### [Subgrid Marching Tetrahedra](1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md)
Reconstructs an intersection-free triangulation by decomposing a regular grid into tetrahedra and solving for the surface within each tetrahedron individually. Unlike its sibling [Marching Cubes](4328-naive-isosurface-extraction.md), which suffers from topological ambiguities in specific configurations, Subgrid MT guarantees a manifold, intersection-free surface by resolving these ambiguities through tetrahedral decomposition. It produces a mesh that matches voxel data more accurately than Marching Cubes, at the cost of a higher vertex count.

### [Canonical Enumeration](1779-canonical-enumeration.md)
The elementary method for cell extraction that sequentially visits all cells in the volume to identify active cells containing the isosurface.

### [Hybrid Memory Constrained Isosurface Extraction](2307-hybrid-memory-constrained-isosurface-extraction.md)
Generates isosurfaces from regularly structured volume data while strictly respecting a prescribed memory limit $M$ for auxiliary data structures. It solves the problem of minimizing expected extraction time by partitioning the volume spatially and assigning one of several extraction methods (enumeration, interval tree, kd-tree, or out-of-core) to each partition block. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Octree-based Isosurfacing](1247-octree-based-isosurfacing.md) by optimizing the *assignment* of extraction algorithms to spatial blocks rather than just the spatial subdivision itself, and from [Streaming Marching Cubes](6190-streaming-marching-cubes.md) by providing a globally optimal solution for a fixed memory budget via Lagrangian optimization.

### [CPU Immediate Mode Marching Cubes](2463-cpu-immediate-mode-marching-cubes.md)
A [classic](#5024-classic-column-voxel-space.md) CPU-based isosurface extraction method that generates mesh vertices and normals in immediate mode, rendering them directly via WebGL draw calls without storing a persistent mesh buffer. It differs from buffered or GPU-accelerated siblings by computing the scalar field and geometry on the [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md) every frame and flushing small batches of primitives directly to the graphics API, making it a valuable reference implementation for comparison.

### [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md)
Provides the static data structures and mapping logic that determine how a voxel's scalar field [sign configuration](#3639-cube-sdf-sampling-and-sign-configuration.md) is converted into mesh geometry. It solves the combinatorial problem of isosurface extraction by replacing runtime conditional branching with direct array indexing, enabling $O(1)$ determination of triangle topology per voxel. It differs from symmetry-based approaches by handling all 256 cases explicitly (or via symmetry reduction) and from dynamic ambiguity resolution methods by using fixed triangulations for ambiguous cases, which may produce topological artifacts if adjacent cells resolve ambiguities inconsistently.

### [Surface Properties and Estimation](2790-surface-properties-and-estimation.md)
Provides methods to compute geometric attributes (normals, area) or improve the visual quality (smoothing) of isosurfaces extracted from scalar fields. It addresses the limitations of raw isosurface extraction, such as jagged artifacts in binary data or the lack of lighting information in mesh generation. It differs from its siblings, which focus on the topology and connectivity of the mesh generation itself, by operating on the resulting geometry or the input field to refine surface representation [30-isosurface-extraction.md].

### [General-purpose Contour Extraction Routine Generator](3666-general-purpose-contour-extraction-routine-generator.md)
A code generator that produces a specialized JavaScript function for extracting surfaces from multi-dimensional `ndarray` data structures. It solves the problem of efficiently traversing grid cells and generating geometric primitives (vertices and faces) based on phase comparisons between adjacent cells. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by decoupling the traversal engine from the surface definition, enabling the generation of arbitrary contouring routines rather than a single fixed algorithm.

### [Surface Tessellation from Iso-Contours](3696-surface-tessellation-from-iso-contours.md)
Represents iso-surfaces by generating polygonal meshes from stacks of 2D contours extracted from consecutive slices of parallel planes within a data volume. It differs from voxel-based methods like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by operating on explicit contour data rather than scalar field samples, and from [Dual Contouring and Surface Nets](6319-dual-contouring-and-surface-nets.md) by relying on inter-slice triangulation of existing boundaries rather than local optimization of vertex positions.

### [THREAD System](3743-thread-system.md)
An early isosurface extraction method that constructs 3D surfaces from a sequence of 2D cross-sectional outlines. It is distinguished from modern grid-based methods (like Marching Cubes) by its reliance on explicit 2D boundary detection and inter-slice interpolation rather than implicit scalar field evaluation on a 3D grid.

### [Preprocessed Marching Cubes](3765-preprocessed-marching-cubes.md)
Extracts a triangle mesh from a 3D scalar volume by applying optional preprocessing steps—such as Gaussian smoothing, connected-component filtering, and boundary darkening—before running the standard Marching Cubes algorithm. Unlike standard Marching Cubes, which operates directly on raw voxel data, this method modifies the input field to ensure topological correctness and robustness against noise.

### [DCX Mesh Extraction via UDF and Marching Cubes](3778-dcx-mesh-extraction-via-udf-and-marching-cubes.md)
Extracts a triangular mesh from a BVH ([Bounding Volume Hierarchy](#2808-domain-based-bvh-with-range-bounding-boxes.md)) structure by computing an Unsigned Distance Field (UDF) on a regular grid, converting it to a Signed Distance Field ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) via flood fill to determine interior/exterior regions, and applying Marching Cubes. It differs from standard Marching Cubes by accepting a BVH as input rather than a pre-computed scalar grid, allowing direct surface extraction from hierarchical geometric representations without intermediate [voxelization](#12-voxelization.md) of the mesh geometry itself.

### [Ground Truth Generation for Neural Marching Cubes](3820-ground-truth-generation-for-neural-marching-cubes.md)
Generates multi-resolution ground truth data for training Neural Marching Cubes (NMC) by computing per-grid-cell labels (case IDs, vertex positions, and plane parameters) from high-resolution voxel and surface intersection data. It differs from gradient-based methods by explicitly using computed surface intersection points and their normals for least-squares fitting to determine plane parameters, rather than relying solely on voxel occupancy or field gradients.

### [Marching Cubes with Narrow-Band Filtering](3826-marching-cubes-with-narrow-band-filtering.md)
Reconstructs a triangle mesh from a Signed Distance Function (SDF) by evaluating the SDF on a regular grid of cubes, filtering out cubes that are too far from the surface (narrow-band filtering), and applying the standard Marching Cubes algorithm only to the intersected cubes. It differs from standard Marching Cubes by skipping non-intersecting cells, significantly reducing computation time for sparse or bounded domains.

### [Marching Cubes with QEF Vertex Optimization](3831-marching-cubes-with-qef-vertex-optimization.md)
Computes vertex positions using a Quadric Error Function (QEF) minimization for ambiguous cases, while using a 2D linear/binomial search for non-ambiguous cases, to produce a watertight mesh from a voxel grid. Unlike standard Marching Cubes which may produce artifacts in ambiguous configurations, this method explicitly solves for vertex positions that minimize distance to the surrounding constraint planes defined by the voxel neighbors.

### [Domain Search Isosurface Extraction](3871-domain-search-isosurface-extraction.md)
Operates on a volumetric grid decomposed into tetrahedra. It determines the isosurface by evaluating the scalar field at the four vertices of each tetrahedron, classifying the cell into one of 16 topological cases based on which vertices lie below a specified isovalue, and generating intersection points via linear interpolation. It differs from standard Marching Cubes by using a tetrahedral decomposition, which avoids the ambiguity issues associated with cube cells, and from dual contouring by producing a triangulated mesh directly from interpolation rather than optimizing vertex positions via quadratic error functions.

### [Digital Surface Extraction via Khalimsky Space](3937-digital-surface-extraction-via-khalimsky-space.md)
Extracts a boundary surface from a digital image by constructing a Khalimsky space, defining a digital set based on intensity thresholds, and scanning the space to identify surfels (surface elements) using a specific adjacency rule (interior or exterior). It differs from [Isosurface extraction](30-isosurface-extraction.md) methods like Marching Cubes by relying on combinatorial topology and digital geometry rather than geometric interpolation within grid cells, ensuring a topologically correct manifold surface.

### [Marching Cubes Job Scheduling](4446-marching-cubes-job-scheduling.md)
A parallel execution strategy for isosurface extraction that decomposes a volumetric dataset into spatial chunks and processes them concurrently using a job system. It solves the performance bottleneck of single-threaded mesh generation by distributing the computational load of vertex and triangle generation across multiple worker threads or processes. Unlike sequential implementations, this method relies on atomic counters for output buffer management and explicit synchronization mechanisms to handle data dependencies between chunk processing and ground truth generation tasks.

### [Marching Cubes Vertex List Generation](4447-marching-cubes-vertex-list-generation.md)
Calculates the precise 3D positions of vertices where a scalar field intersects the edges of a voxel grid cell, based on a specified isovalue. It serves as the geometric foundation for polygonal mesh generation by determining *where* the surface cuts through a cube, distinct from the topological decision of *which* triangles to form [30-isosurface-extraction.md]. Unlike [Marching Cubes Surface Point Extraction](6417-marching-cubes-surface-point-extraction.md), which aggregates multiple intersections into a single representative point per voxel for point-based rendering, this method generates a distinct vertex for every intersected edge to preserve topological connectivity for meshing.

### [Incremental Contouring via Power Diagrams](4955-incremental-contouring-via-power-diagrams.md)
A progressive isosurface extraction algorithm that constructs a mesh from a Signed Distance Field (SDF) by iteratively refining a weighted triangulation (regular triangulation or power diagram). Unlike static methods like Marching Cubes or Dual Contouring that operate on a fixed grid, this method starts with a coarse set of samples and incrementally inserts new vertices at locations of high geometric deviation, updating the local triangulation and surface mesh without global recomputation. It leverages the dual relationship between power diagrams and regular Delaunay tetrahedralizations to ensure topological correctness and geometric fidelity, particularly for complex or high-genus surfaces.

### [Gallagher-Nagtegaal Bicubic Method](5321-gallagher-nagtegaal-bicubic-method.md)
Replaces the triangular primitives of Marching Cubes with visually continuous bicubic polynomial patches. It solves the problem of geometric discontinuity and aliasing artifacts inherent in piecewise-linear approximations by providing a smooth, curved representation of the implicit surface. Unlike its sibling [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md), which outputs a mesh of triangles, this method outputs a set of parametric surface patches, making it particularly suitable for applications requiring high visual fidelity or further subdivision. It builds on [Isosurface extraction](30-isosurface-extraction.md) by maintaining the cell-based traversal logic but altering the primitive generation step to fit a bicubic function rather than a linear interpolation.

### [Marching Cubes on Structured Grids](6051-marching-cubes-on-structured-grids.md)

### [Streaming Marching Cubes](6190-streaming-marching-cubes.md)
Extracts isosurfaces from volumetric datasets by combining memory-efficient streaming processing with explicit vertex sharing to ensure topological consistency. It solves the problem of generating watertight, shared-vertex meshes from massive data that cannot fit entirely in memory, while avoiding the vertex duplication common in naive streaming implementations. It differs from standard [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md) by explicitly managing vertex identity across cell boundaries via a hash table, and from [Sparse Marching Cubes](3825-sparse-marching-cubes.md) by focusing on the streaming memory constraint rather than spatial sparsity.

### [Transvoxel](6277-transvoxel.md)
A level-of-detail (LOD) technique for isosurface extraction that maintains a watertight mesh when neighboring voxels in a hierarchical grid have different resolutions. It solves the gap problem inherent in standard [LOD transitions](#4459-transvoxel-transition-face-generation.md) by introducing transition cells that interpolate vertices between coarse and fine grids, ensuring continuity across resolution boundaries. Unlike standard Marching Cubes which assumes uniform voxel size, [Transvoxel](#6277-transvoxel.md) adapts vertex positions and normals based on the LOD of adjacent voxels.

### [Dual Contouring and Surface Nets](6319-dual-contouring-and-surface-nets.md)
Generate a single vertex per active grid cell (voxel) rather than placing vertices on cell edges like Marching Cubes [G]. This family prioritizes mesh sparsity and feature preservation over topological simplicity, producing watertight meshes with fewer triangles [G]. Dual Contouring optimizes vertex position via a Quadratic Error Function (QEF) to preserve sharp features [778-dual-contouring.md], while Surface Nets uses a weighted average of intersection points for a faster, normal-free approximation [921-surface-nets.md].

### [Neural and Learning-based Extraction](6371-neural-and-learning-based-extraction.md)
Extracts triangle meshes from neural implicit representations (occupancy fields, SDFs, or [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) densities) by combining neural query capabilities with geometric extraction algorithms. It solves the problem of converting continuous, learned volumetric functions into explicit polygonal meshes suitable for rendering or simulation. Unlike static methods like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) on fixed grids, this family distinguishes itself by either adaptively querying the neural network to save computation (e.g., [MISE](#977-mise-meshing-isosurfaces-by-extracting.md)) or by making the extraction process fully differentiable to allow gradient-based optimization of the mesh geometry (e.g., [FlexiCubes](#3669-flexicubes.md)).

### [Two-Step Surface Reconstruction Method](7364-two-step-surface-reconstruction-method.md)
Accelerates Marching Cubes by using a lower expansion order FMM evaluation to filter non-boundary voxels, then using a higher expansion order FMM evaluation only on potential boundary voxels to extract the isosurface.

### [Adaptive Minimum Projected Size Adjustment](7457-adaptive-minimum-projected-size-adjustment.md)
Automatically adjusts the minimum projected size of surface elements frame-to-frame to maintain a target framerate during user [interaction](#41-interaction.md), preventing poor or over-populated geometry at varying camera distances.

### [Non-reconnected Multiresolution Isosurfacing](7512-non-reconnected-multiresolution-isosurfacing.md)
Intentionally omits surface reconnection between adjacent cells of different resolutions to avoid tracking overhead, relying on sufficient polygon density to keep cracks visually negligible.

### [Region-growing Iso-surface Extraction](7568-region-growing-iso-surface-extraction.md)
A [region-growing based iso-surface extraction algorithm](#7568-region-growing-iso-surface-extraction.md) that generates high-quality curvature-adaptive semi-regular meshes, preserves sharp features, and extracts all disjoint components of the iso-surface.

### [Generalized Marching Cubes](8320-generalized-marching-cubes.md)
A contouring method applied to generate triangulated mesh surfaces from the classified volumetric model, capable of dealing with both CT values and material types.

### [Grid Traversal and Data Structure Adaptation](8340-grid-traversal-and-data-structure-adaptation.md)
Extracts isosurfaces from scalar fields by adapting the underlying spatial data structure to the geometry, rather than iterating over a fixed uniform grid. By using hierarchical structures like octrees or sparse hash maps, these algorithms reduce memory usage and computational cost by only processing cells where the surface exists or varies significantly. They set themselves apart from sibling methods like [Transvoxel](6277-transvoxel.md) by relying on standard topological triangulation rules (e.g., Marching Cubes) applied to adapted domains, often requiring specific traversal logic to handle mismatched refinement levels between adjacent cells.

### [Visualization and Rendering Techniques](8434-visualization-and-rendering-techniques.md)

### [GPU and Shader-Based Extraction](9036-gpu-and-shader-based-extraction.md)
Encompasses methods that perform isosurface extraction primarily on the GPU using shader programs, often leveraging parallel processing architectures to accelerate the evaluation of implicit functions and the generation of geometric primitives. Unlike traditional CPU-based approaches that may suffer from memory transfer bottlenecks or limited parallelism, these methods utilize the GPU's massive parallelism for tasks such as distance evaluation, voxel traversal, and mesh generation. They differ from their siblings by explicitly offloading the computational heavy lifting to the graphics pipeline, often using render-to-vertex-array techniques or specialized compute shaders to bypass the CPU-GPU data transfer latency [3818-gpu-accelerated-marching-cubes-with-distance-extraction.md], [6862-gpu-isosurface-extraction-from-molecular-orbital-densities.md], [7507-fragment-shader-isosurface-extraction-with-mrts.md].

### [DCx (Dual Contouring over Expanded Cubes)](9342-dcx-dual-contouring-over-expanded-cubes.md)
An extension of the standard Dual Contouring algorithm designed to extract zero-level sets from neural Unsigned Distance Functions (UDFs). It addresses the lack of sign information in UDFs by using an optimization-based strategy for active cube detection and operating on 2x2x2 voxel blocks (expanded cubes) to support non-manifold structures.

#### Point Cloud Extraction
Converts isosurfaces to point clouds by evaluating chunks of voxels and extracting vertices at the center of edges where the isosurface passes, without generating face data [S8, unofficial]. Unlike surface reconstruction methods, this method does not contain any surface data; surfaces have to be reconstructed, ideally on the GPU itself [S8, unofficial].

#### Fast Marching-Cubes-Style Volume Evaluation
An efficient and accurate volume evaluation method for grid-based level sets that computes the volume of implicitly represented shapes consistent with Marching Cubes surface reconstruction [S9, unofficial]. It utilizes rotational symmetry to combine redundant Marching Cubes cases and avoids explicitly forming local triangulations using efficient volume computation formulae for pyramids and truncated prisms wherever possible, thereby achieving a fast and compact implementation [S9, unofficial]. The method achieves second-order accuracy convergence and results perfectly consistent with volumes calculated directly from explicit Marching Cubes meshes [S9, unofficial].

#### Mask-based Cutaways
A strategy for making inner contour surfaces visible by specifying which cells contribute to the contour surface using a mask [S10]. Only cells for which the mask value is true at all eight vertices contribute to the contour surface. The mask argument can also specify separate masks for each level as a list of logical arrays or functions [S10].

#### Fuzzy Metaballs to Mesh Export
A pipeline to convert a Fuzzy Metaballs algebraic surface model into a polygonal mesh by optimizing the extraction threshold against silhouette fidelity [S11]. Differs from fixed-threshold extraction by dynamically adjusting the threshold via optimization, preserving silhouette fidelity at the cost of an extra optimization step [S11]. Used in experiments to compare Fuzzy Metaballs against equivalent mesh (170 faces, 85 vertices) and point cloud (430 points) representations [S11].

#### Cuberille
A technique for visualizing volumes by drawing each voxel as a small cube [S12]. It finds every voxel with a value greater than 0 (assuming isovalue t=0) and draws a cube, selecting only those cube faces which separate cubes that are inside (t<0) from cubes that are outside (t>=0), then stitching the selected faces together to form a quad mesh [S12]. Ambiguous configuration where four faces meet at an edge is resolved by deciding which pair of faces to stitch together using the [asymptotic decider](#790-asymptotic-decider.md) by Nielson and Hamann [S12].

#### Mesh Extraction via Marching Cubes
Creating a simplified proxy mesh from 3D Gaussians to determine page affiliations and facilitate page linking, using Marching Cubes for efficiency [S13]. It defines a plane normal to the Z-axis to create a slice of the scene, intersects this plane with the scene and renders it as an image, and repeats the process while moving the plane along the Z-axis in fixed steps for subsequent slices [S13]. Morphological operations are performed on the data before surface reconstruction to make the mesh coarser, close small holes, and reduce unnecessary details [S13].

#### 4D Marching Cubes
Extends Marching Cubes into 4 dimensions. The resulting look-up table requires 222 separate configurations after removal of symmetrical configurations [S14, unofficial]. Dealing with ambiguous configurations is a consideration; a mathematical proof of correctness is provided to verify that the topological structures generated are valid [S14, unofficial]. Used by Bhaniramka et al. [76] to present volume data with a time dimension by selecting three-dimensional slices of the hyper-volume [S14, unofficial].

#### Multi-Isosurface Rendering
IR renders a surface in 3D space that intersects voxels having a constant value (isosurface), similar to a 2D isocontour [S15]. It performs isosurface extraction offline as a preprocessing step given a volumetric data set, extracts a set of isosurfaces at uniformly chosen isovalues from the data set, identifies a small subset of these isosurfaces as representatives, and renders the output triangle primitives of the selected isosurfaces using a simple [Blinn-Phong illumination model](#2239-blinn-phong-shading-model.md) [S15]. For IR, the normalized isovalue is used as a texture coordinate to index into the shared [color transfer function](#6581-color-based-transfer-function.md) to assign a color for the isosurface [S15].

#### Marching Cubes Tetrahedron Decomposition
A variant that applies the [Marching Tetrahedrons algorithm](#940-marching-tetrahedrons-algorithm.md) to a cube by decomposing the cube into 6 tetrahedrons, aiming to resolve topological ambiguities inherent in standard Marching Cubes [S16, unofficial]. Compared to standard `MarchCube`, this method is slower and creates more vertices but better represents the mesh surface by avoiding ambiguous cases [S16, unofficial].

#### Differentiable Marching Cubes
A differentiable meshing algorithm that divides 3D space into a deformable grid and takes a scalar field (often SDF) defined on its vertices as input to generate an explicit watertight manifold mesh [S17]. DiffMC produces significantly smoother surfaces and mitigates artifacts from density field non-linearity compared to DMTet, which produces zigzag lines [S17]. Rendering quality (PSNR) improves with DiffMC resolution, plateauing around 400. At resolution 256, PSNR is 31.19; at 400, PSNR is 31.54 [S17].

## Background
The Marching Cubes algorithm was introduced by Lorensen & Cline in 1987 [S3, unofficial]. It is a general approach covering a whole family of algorithms, some of which are adaptive, supplemented with sharp feature detection, or capable of preserving the topology of non-manifold surfaces [S1, S5, unofficial]. Conceptually, contouring is simple: cover the plane with a grid, measure function signs in every corner for each square, and add line segments accordingly [S5, unofficial]. Since pairs of signs for each shared edge change synchronously for both cells, the line segments connect automatically into a continuous contour [S5, unofficial]. Linear interpolation is used to find the exact position of the line segment ends on the edges, rather than placing them at the middle, though this is an approximation because the target function is not necessarily linear [S5, unofficial]. The error of the simple contour (middle-to-middle) never exceeds half of the cell's diagonal [S1, S5, unofficial].
